title: DD's measured effectiveness lives in the agent trial, and its time gain is one outlier
body:
Quote the agent trial from output/eval/agent-results.json (claude-sonnet-5, 6 tasks x 3 repeats, fresh clone per run, 2026-09-23): 15/18 passed without DD, 18/18 with DD, cost about equal (7.02 vs 7.13 USD). Do not claim a speedup from its summary minutes (72.4 vs 37.3): nearly all of that gap is the retrieve-title task, where one no-DD run hit the 25-minute timeout and another took 11 minutes; other tasks took similar time. Disclose the bias: the tasks were picked because a memory holds what the code does not show (commit 6cb6acd). agent-results-pruned.json is the DD condition with some memories removed (16/18), not a no-DD baseline. The 84% token saving comes from authored replay scenarios and measures context cost, not task success.

Why: No document cites this trial: docs/evaluation/model-evaluation.md still calls quality and speed gains hypotheses, so an agent asked for evidence either misses it or reads the summary block and reports a 2x speedup that one timeout produces.

evidence.summary: summary without_dd 15/18 passed, 72.4 min, 7.0163 USD; with_dd 18/18, 37.3 min, 7.1337 USD; retrieve-title no-DD rows include a 25.0 min timeout and an 11.0 min run
with_dd only, 16/18 passed, no without_dd runs
line 84 says cross-model quality and development-speed gains remain hypotheses to measure; the agent trial is not mentioned
harness: fresh clone per run, headless Claude Code, 20-minute timeout, DD condition adds hooks and MCP server

revisit_when.description: A new agent trial run replaces these numbers

v1.trigger: When stating whether DD measurably helps (README, release notes, posts, docs/evaluation), or quoting the with-DD vs without-DD agent trial numbers
